merger_description:
Sanad Services Group owned by One Hundred and Seven Investment RSC LTD – Sole Proprietorship L.L.C. (**Sanad Services**) and Ace Aéro Partenaires II S.L.P. (**AAP2**) (an investment fund) propose to acquire Revima Holding SAS (**Revima**).

Revima supplies maintenance, repair and overhaul (**MRO**) services for aircraft auxiliary power units (**APUs**) and aircraft landing gear systems. Revima also supplies, to a more limited extent, MRO services for engine parts (but not MRO services for complete engines). Revima services customers globally from its MRO facilities in France and Thailand.

Sanad Services supplies MRO services for aircraft engines and related aftermarket services. Sanad Services provides these services to customers globally from its facilities in the UAE. Samad Services is ultimately owned by Mubadala Investment Company PJSC (**MIC**), a UAE public joint stock company wholly owned by the Government of Abu Dhabi.

AAP2 is an investment fund represented by Tikehau Investment Management SAS (**TIM**), in its capacity as management company. TIM is itself a wholly owned subsidiary of Tikehau Capital SCA, the parent company of the Tikehau Capital group, a France-based global asset management and investment group (**Tikehau Capital**).

determination_table_content.details:
Sanad Services Group, owned by One Hundred and Seven
Investment RSC LTD – Sole Proprietorship L.L.C. (Sanad Services)
and Ace Aéro Partenaires II S.L.P. (AAP2) (an investment fund)
propose to acquire Revima Holding SAS (Revima) (the Acquisition).
The Acquisition would result in Sanad Services and AAP2 obtaining
joint control of Revima through a joint special purpose vehicle,
Dream BidCo.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABZE(1) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition may be put into effect.

Sanad Services supplies maintenance, repair and overhaul services
for aircraft engines and related aftermarket services. Sanad Services
provides these services to customers globally from its facilities in
the UAE. Sanad Services is ultimately owned by Mubadala
Investment Company PJSC (MIC), a UAE public joint stock company
wholly owned by the Government of Abu Dhabi.
AAP2 is an investment fund represented by Tikehau Investment
Management SAS (TIM), in its capacity as management company.
TIM is itself a wholly owned subsidiary of Tikehau Capital SCA, the
parent company of the Tikehau Capital group, a France-based global
asset management and investment group.
The target, Revima, supplies maintenance, repair and overhaul
services for aircraft auxiliary power units and aircraft landing gear
systems. Revima also supplies, to a more limited extent,
maintenance, repair and overhaul services for engine parts (but not
for complete engines). Revima services customers globally from its
facilities in France and Thailand.

determination_table_content.item:
Overlap and relationship
between the Parties
determination_table_content.details:
Revima supplies some maintenance, repair and overhaul services for
individual engine parts.
Sanad Services supplies maintenance, repair and overhaul services
for complete engines.
Providers of engine maintenance, repair and overhaul services may,
at times, outsource such services in respect of certain individual
engine parts. However, there is no current subcontracting
relationship between Sanad Services and Revima.

When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form and information from third parties.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market in
Australia. In reaching its decision, and based on the material before
it, the ACCC makes the following findings.
• There is minimal overlap between Sanad Services and Revima
and they are not close competitors in the supply of maintenance,
repair and overhaul services.
• Although engine parts maintenance, repair and overhaul services
may be supplied as an input to engine services, the Acquisition
would be unlikely to give rise to vertical effects, because there
are multiple alternative suppliers of both engine maintenance,
repair and overhaul services and engine parts maintenance,
repair and overhaul services. Therefore, the merged entity would
be unlikely to have the ability and incentive to foreclose rivals in
either service offering.

A notifying party, or other person who has been allowed to do so by
the Australian Competition Tribunal, may apply for review if they are
dissatisfied with the determination. Pursuant to section 100C of the
Act, applications for review of the determination are to be made to
the Australian Competition Tribunal before the end of 14 calendar
days after this statement of reasons was included on the ACCC’s
Acquisitions Register. To confirm whether there has been any
application for review, please contact the Australian Competition
Tribunal.
